page: Amazon Web Services c7a.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and fourth-generation AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 96 dedicated physical cores running at up to 3.7 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 192 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5000 MHz, providing a strict 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware-level acceleration includes AVX-512 vector instructions with VNNI and BF16 support, as well as dedicated cryptographic extensions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark testing demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded throughput. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 106,489.34 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 22,509.0, excelling notably in code compilation with Clang (79,149.0) and ray tracing tasks (111,703.0). Memory subsystems show high cached read bandwidth of 12,128.93 GB/sec and uncached read speeds of 348.43 GB/sec. In distributed caching environments, the configuration demonstrates extreme operational scale, delivering 172.4 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations.

Network performance is backed by a 38 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for persistent data persistence. Furthermore, no discrete GPUs are present, though CPU-based LLM inference metrics register strong prompt processing and token generation rates on small and medium models through vector execution units.

From an infrastructure cost efficiency standpoint, the c7a.24xlarge maximizes throughput per core by offering completely non-hyperthreaded physical cores paired with DDR5 channels. This architecture minimizes noisy-neighbor contention and optimizes computational density for CPU-bound applications. The platform is well suited for high-performance computing, large-scale software builds, batch video and physics rendering, distributed analytics engines, and static web serving tiers.
description: Amazon Web Services c7a.24xlarge is a high-performance compute-optimized server powered by 96 dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 physical cores running at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 192 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, it delivers a 2 GB per core ratio optimized for CPU-intensive parallel applications. It includes support for AVX-512 extensions and standard cryptographic instruction sets. Networking is anchored by a 38 Gbps baseline bandwidth, while local storage is not bundled, relying on external network volumes. Benchmark figures show top-tier multi-core execution across PassMark, Geekbench, and Redis key-value workloads. With zero GPU acceleration, it relies entirely on high-frequency, non-hyperthreaded CPU silicon. This platform fits distributed scientific computing, intensive CI/CD compilation pipelines, batch processing, and high-throughput web serving environments.
